opportunities.name: arXiv topic search → Semantic Scholar citation lookup → note
opportunities.description: For a given research topic and year, run an arXiv advanced search filtered to that year, open a top result, look up its title on Semantic Scholar to get the first author and citation count, and save a note with the summary.
steps: On arXiv, click Search, then Advanced search
Enter the topic in 'Search term...'
Check the date filter checkbox, select 'specific_year' and enter the year
Click Search and open the top relevant result
Copy the paper title
On Semantic Scholar, search for the exact title and open the matching paper
Read the first author and citation count
In Notes, add a new note: '<topic> (<year>): <title> by <first author>, <N> citations'

instances.values: topic='retrieval augmented generation', year=2023 → RIGHT: Retrieval-augmented Generation for Mainstream Hashtag Recommendation (Run-Ze Fan, 11 citations); a weather lookup interrupted it
topic='protein structure diffusion', year=2024 → Accelerating Inference in Molecular Diffusion Models... (Ian Dunn, 7 citations)
topic='graph neural networks traffic forecasting', year=2022 → Efficient Traffic State Forecasting... (Bin Lei, 1 citation); the flowers/email work interrupted it

opportunities.name: Case law citation + related statute → note
opportunities.description: For a given court case name, find it on CourtListener to get its reporter citation and decision date, look up the related U.S. Code section on Cornell LII, and save a note that links the two.
steps: On CourtListener, go to Case Law → Search Case Law
Enter the case name in 'Keyword(s) search with operators' and press Enter
Open the matching case and note its citation and decision date
On Cornell LII, search for the related U.S.C. section and open it
Note the section title
In Notes, add a new note: '<case>: <citation>, decided <date>. See <U.S.C. section> (<section title>)'

instances.values: Carpenter v. United States → 585 U.S. 296, June 22, 2018; 18 U.S.C. 2703
Bostock v. Clayton County → 590 U.S. 644, June 15, 2020; 42 U.S.C. 2000e-2
Miranda v. Arizona → 384 U.S. 436, June 13, 1966; 18 U.S.C. 3501

opportunities.name: Event planning: venue search + flowers + summary email
opportunities.description: For an event type, city, guest count and date, search Peerspace for venues, search 1-800-Flowers for a flower arrangement, and draft an email to the organizer that summarizes the venue, catering and flowers.
steps: On Peerspace, clear and enter the activity in 'Enter your activity'
Clear and enter the city in 'Enter a city, zip, or address', then pick the autocomplete option
Click Search and review the venue results and prices
On 1-800-Flowers, search for the flower type and open a product to get its name and price
In Mail, compose to the recipient with subject '<event> on <date>: venue, food, flowers'
Write a body that summarizes the guest count, venue rate, catering minimum and flower product/price
Send the email (or save it as a draft)

instances.values: event='Team offsite', city=Chicago (only the Peerspace search; it took several retries)
event='Birthday party', city=San Francisco, flowers='tulips' (no email seen)
event='Product launch', city=New York, flowers='white orchids' → White Phalaenopsis Orchid $59.99; email to priya@example.com, Jan 14, 60 guests (discarded)
